newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Genome sees 2 deals by year end.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Genome sees 2 deals by year end.

text.p: Genome Therapeutics Corp is in talks with pharmaceutical companies that could lead to two new partnership deals by the end of the year, the company's chief executive said on Tuesday.

The deals could involve the company's first pact involving genetic information on a human disease and its third dealing with a disease-causing pathogen, Robert Hennessey, Genome Therapeutics chief executive officer said in an interview.
"We still feel confident we can do that," Hennessey said of the company's goal for two deals by year end.
In 1995 Genome Therapeutics signed a pact with AB Astra aimed at speeding up discovery of treatments for ulcers caused by the helicobacter pylori bacteria.
It also signed a deal last year with Schering-Plough Corp for development of treatments against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

The two deals have a potential worth of $65.5 million to Genome Therapeutics, which is involved in identifying human genes responsible for genetic diseases and bacterial genes behind infectious diseases.

Hennessey said Genome Therapeutics is working on a deal for the end of the year that would provide a pharmaceutical company partner exclusive access to Genome Therapeutics' genetic information on a specific human disease.
The possible disease targets include osteoporosis, asthma, prostate cancer, schizophrenia and manic depression, he said.

The other pact would likely involve a company gaining non-exclusive access to genetic information on a pathogen. Such a deal could eventually lead to an exclusive agreement involving information on specific genetic targets for attacking the pathogen, Hennessey said.
He said his objective was to have a second human disease deal and "a couple" more pathogen deals in 1997.
